question.q: Is Oracle Streams still an option for replicating to Azure?
question.expected: No: desupported in Oracle Database 19c (deprecated since 12.1); name the replacement route (GoldenGate or a log-based CDC tool / Azure DMS where applicable).

result:
**Verdict: No — Oracle Streams is desupported and not usable as a replication option; use Oracle GoldenGate or an Azure-side CDC pipeline instead.**

**Oracle-side status**
Oracle Streams (introduced pre-11.2) was **deprecated in 12.1** and **desupported starting 19.1 (19c)**, with Oracle naming **GoldenGate** as the replacement. Oracle's notice also states it never supported multitenant, and that Advanced Queuing (the underlying queuing mechanism) itself remains fully supported. — [Deprecated and Desupported Features for Oracle Database 12c (12.1)](https://docs.oracle.com/database/121/UPGRD/deprecated.htm), [Oracle Database Changes, Desupports, and Deprecations (Upgrade Guide 19c)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/19/upgrd/oracle-database-changes-deprecations-desupports.html)

**What the dataset maps Streams to on Azure (scoped to Oracle 11.2–18c, since Streams predates its own desupport there):**

- **Azure Database Migration Service** — fidelity **none**. DMS has no online/continuous-sync scenario with Oracle as a source (Oracle→Azure SQL is offline-only via SSMA; no Oracle→PostgreSQL scenario exists), so it can't substitute for Streams replication. Severity: **blocker**. — [Azure Database Migration Service: supported migration scenarios](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/dms/resource-scenario-status)
- **Azure Data Factory** — fidelity **workaround**, effort L. ADF's Oracle connector is batch-only; Oracle isn't in ADF's native CDC or auto-incremental connector lists, so you'd build a customer-managed watermark pipeline — scheduled micro-batches, not log-based streaming, and no delete capture without a soft-delete column. Severity: **major**. — [Change data capture in Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/concepts-change-data-capture), [Copy data to and from Oracle with Azure Data Factory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/data-factory/connector-oracle)
- **Microsoft Fabric (Mirroring)** — fidelity **partial**, effort M. Fabric mirrors Oracle via LogMiner into Delta tables in OneLake (latency as low as tens of seconds), reproducing capture-and-apply for analytics — but it's one-directional into OneLake only, requires archive log mode, supplemental logging, and an on-prem data gateway. It cannot replicate into another Oracle or SQL database. Severity: **major** (prerequisites). — [Mirror Oracle databases in Microsoft Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/mirroring/oracle), [Mirroring in Microsoft Fabric](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/mirroring/overview)
- **Oracle Database@Azure** — fidelity **partial**, effort M. Since Streams is desupported, the Oracle-native successor here is **GoldenGate**, which Microsoft lists as a monitored deployment type for active-active replication with app-level conflict handling — but GoldenGate is **not included** in Oracle Database@Azure pricing and requires separate licensing; its capture/replicat config differs from Streams rules. Severity: **major**. — [Overview: Oracle Database@Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/oracle/oracle-db/database-overview), [Business continuity and disaster recovery for Oracle Database@Azure (Exadata Database Service)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/oracle-on-azure/oracle-disaster-recovery-oracle-database-azure)

**Bottom line for migration design:** none of the four Azure-side targets are a true drop-in for Streams' database-to-database log-based replication. For operational replication, the dataset points to **GoldenGate** (self-licensed, on Oracle Database@Azure or elsewhere); for analytics-oriented CDC into Azure, **Fabric Mirroring** is the closest (partial) fit; ADF is a workaround at best; DMS is not viable at all for this purpose.

No `dispute` entries were found for Oracle Streams in the dataset.
